data.head: ## What crosses (read in the merged tree)

body: - **Drops from other applications (`82a6573ee`):** `packages/blitz-shell/src/dnd.rs` turns winit's drag events into `UiEvent::DragEnter/DragOver/DragLeave/Drop` carrying a `DataTransfer` (`packages/blitz-traits/src/events/datatransfer.rs`): strings by type, files as `PathBuf`s from `file://` URIs (`dnd.rs:293`, `file_uri_to_path`). `packages/blitz-dom/src/events/driver.rs:191-407` dispatches `dragenter`/`dragover`/`dragleave`/`drop` to the page in every document. In dioxus-native-dom a dropped file is read from disk on an app handler's ask — `std::fs::metadata`, `std::fs::read`, `std::fs::read_to_string`, `std::fs::File::open` (merged `events.rs`, the `NativeFileData` impl) — no path restriction. A page script's document (blitz-vibey-script) hears the four events by name through `create_event(… data.name() …)` (`packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/event.rs:242`) with no data transfer filled. The only source is a windowed shell or an in-process caller of `handle_ui_event`: no harness input, driver verb, MCP tool or stand task reaches it (`git grep` of `DragEnter|Drop(` over `packages/blitz-test-harness`, `packages/escher-driver`, `examples/seven_guis`: 0 hits).

- **The file-drop example (`29a439e05`):** `examples/file_drop.rs` reads a dropped directory, metadata and up to its preview bound of a text file through `std::fs`, and previews an image or HTML file as a `file:` URL in an `img` or `iframe` (`file_drop.rs:200-206`); in this fork a `file:` sub-resource of a non-`file:` document is refused before any disk read (security · decision/file-url-only-for-file-documents), so those two previews are refused here — read from the code, not run (the example is windowed). `examples/dnd.rs` prints its events with `println!` (an example's stdout, no `tracing` site).

- **One-axis `overflow: clip` (`f65baeca5`):** `clipped_axes` in `packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs` clips paint only on the clipped axis for `overflow: clip`; a scroll container, replaced content, a text input and paint containment still clip both. Paint now agrees with `visible_region`'s one-axis narrowing; the hit still stops at the whole padding box (`packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:1678-1688`), as architecture · decision/one-axis-clip-readings-kept states. Screenshot pixels of such a box change; no stand screen and no guarded reading moved (the tests above).

Not tested | **Keep out.** It does not merge without pain: a lock regeneration (`--locked` refuses it as it stands) and a git dependency, which T2 A now makes a new ruling of its own |

## 2. One-axis `overflow: clip`: paint and hit now differ by design
- With C1 A, `clipped_axes` (`packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:344`, used `:395`, `:498`) clips paint only on the clipped axis for `overflow: clip`. Paint now agrees with `visible_region` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/scrolling.rs:816`).

- Drops from other applications enter only through blitz-shell's windowed source (`packages/blitz-shell/src/dnd.rs`) or an in-process caller of `handle_ui_event` with `UiEvent::DragOver` / `DragLeave` / `Drop`.

- Read from the code, not run: the example is windowed.

- Platform: accesskit_xplat adapters (windows, macos, unix, android, null); ActionRequested and AccessibilityDeactivated are unhandled TODOs; no keyboard or assistive-technology route to drag and drop exists, a drag reaching a document only as OS pointer drop input; the tree is built on InitialTreeRequested and pushed again in a redraw, after style resolve, only when the document's changed set, taken and cleared by that redraw, was non-empty, a poll pushing no tree — a focus move (a focus lost after layout too), a checked change, a rewritten name, a text control's input, a select's changed choice, a single select's list opening or closing and other mutations mark it, a page scroll or a move that closes a list marking its select through `reconcile_select_list` at the next resolve and a wheel elsewhere through `close_select_list`, and its highlight moving to another row marking it too, while a wheel move inside a list marks nothing and a pointer move alone does not — through `Document::accessibility_tree` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-07; before 2026-10-07 the poll-time refresh never ran; no windowed witness on the dev host — still owed at the platform adapter, the stand building no adapter, kept so on the founder's F1 (2026-10-14), and owned by residual `res-llkgqygv` (re-carried at 0.3.0, target: next), an active assistive technology this version does not reach; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions both halves are proven headlessly on the stand in both layout modes: on Counter, after a drained changed set, each Tab of the whole `tab_order` and an Enter on `counter-increment` leave `has_changes()` true, and the tree read through `&dyn Document` reads the new focus stop and `counter-value`'s new name). A harness settle neither reads nor drains that changed set, and the set is non-empty on a freshly booted harness document — a check reading the flag as "this step changed something" drains first. Names come from text children, a trimmed-non-empty `aria-label` and `<label>` association (`for`-target, else first nested labelable element — a `button`, an `input` whose `type` is not `hidden`, a `meter`, `output`, `progress`, `select` or `textarea`; a hidden input is named by no label); since 2026-10-17-upstream-sync-engine-debts an `aria-labelledby` whose targets hold text outranks both (accname 2B) — its loop runs after the `<label>` → input loop, clears `labelled_by` and pushes the referenced nodes, the `aria-label` staying the fallback when the targets hold none — and that text reaches the snapshot `name`. The seven_guis stand names no `accessibility` feature in its own manifest — dioxus-native-dom's reaches it through escher-driver, so both its binaries compile the accessibility modules — and builds no platform adapter (`accesskit_xplat` and `accesskit_winit` in neither graph), so the stand binary gives no assistive technology a tree; re-read at 2026-10-10-mcp-surface, when escher-driver took `serde_json` as a fourth dependency (one lock line, no package), no platform adapter joins the stand graph.
- Stylo 0.24, Taffy 0.16 (the crates.io registry; every dependency a registry version, no git source) via `stylo_taffy`, Parley 0.13 (registry), ICU4X 2.3, accesskit (feature `accessibility`).

- `UiEvent` (its drag variants `DragOver` — DOM dragenter and dragover to the node under the drag — `DragLeave` — dragleave, also when the drag leaves the document — and `Drop` — drop to the node under the drag, a drop effect taking only where the drag source allows it), `DomEvent`, `DomEventKind` (`from_str` strips `on`, maps `composition` to `Ime` and `change` to `Change`; `DomEventKind::Change`, after `Input`, and `DomEventData::Change(BlitzInputEvent)` — named `change`, not cancelable, bubbling, with no UI event mapped and no default action — dispatched by blitz-dom after `input` on a select's choice and on a checkbox's or radio's click, a radio only where it was not checked before, a text or range input firing no engine `change`), `EventState`, `BlitzPointerId`, the DataTransfer model — `BlitzDataTransfer` (string and file items with their types and files, `effectAllowed` and `dropEffect`, and a store mode, the operations named by `BlitzDragOperation` and `BlitzDragOperations`) — per-event `cancelable()` / `bubbles()` tables, `BlitzImeEvent`, `BlitzDragEvent` (the pointer coordinates and the shared data transfer of a drag).

- DOM events route to the vdom via the nearest `data-dioxus-id` attribute (parsed as `usize`); where a `SignalRegistry` stands at `ScopeId::ROOT` (`runtime.has_context`), `DioxusEventHandler::handle_event` sets its dispatch — the chain head first, and its event name — around `runtime.handle_event` and clears it after, so a signal write is recorded against the dispatch that caused it, while a page with no registered state dispatches as before; it resolves the reached record (`record_reached`, `reached_handlers`) by stable id before the handlers run and writes it after — every listening node of the chain while the event propagates, the innermost alone when a listener stops it or a handler's panic unwinds, a non-bubbling event's target alone — only where that was switched on, inert elsewhere at one `has_context` lookup per dispatch; listener registration sets a `"<rust func>"` placeholder; drag events reach the app as `NativeDragData`, which implements Dioxus's `NativeDataTransfer`, `HasFileData`, `HasDataTransferData`, `HasDragData` and `ModifiersInteraction`, so a drag handler reads the data transfer, the dropped files and the keyboard modifiers; `Input | Change` reach the app as `NativeFormData { value }`, `multiple_select_values` filling `values` with one `(name, FormValue::Text(value))` per chosen option of a `multiple` select so `evt.values()` reads the set while `value` stays `select_value`, so a select's `onchange` handler fires — and since Dioxus writes a dynamic `selected` again on each re-render, a controlled app writes `selected` from its `input` event's value or a choice reverts.
| Layout | Taffy 0.16 (crates.io registry, no git source; std, flexbox, flexbox_balance, grid, block_layout, content_size, calc, detailed_layout_info) via `stylo_taffy` |

This project was adopted into the Andromeda pipeline (`/andromeda-adopt` at `0f60502e`); its masters describe the code as built. Upstream DioxusLabs/blitz `main` was last merged at `23b9b26a9` (merge commit `3eda07bc`, 2026-10-17), the next sync's merge base; upstream `main` was last read at `563d3db73`, an upstream sync merging DioxusLabs/blitz main with two parents, every upstream commit left out named with its reason, the twenty-nine commits of that take ratified as engine behaviour changes for every document (Taffy now 0.16 from crates.io, no git source); Dioxus is held at 0.7.3, the Dioxus 0.8 move kept out of the upstream take.

**What breaks:** bumping one side of a coupled pin fails to build or mis-renders.
**How to avoid:** markup5ever/html5ever/xml5ever must match stylo's `web_atoms`; skrifa must match parley (the renderer set may bring a second skrifa and read-fonts version beside it); svgtypes must match usvg; taffy is Taffy 0.16.0 from crates.io and parley a registry version (0.13), the manifest admitting no git source; winit is exact `=0.31.0-beta.4`. Bump the set together.
**References:** arch §Established Decisions [Dependency pinning]

**Stack:** Rust 2024 Cargo workspace 0.3.0-beta.4 (rust-version 1.91.0, no `rust-toolchain.toml`) · Stylo 0.24 · Taffy 0.16 (crates.io) · Parley 0.13 · anyrender 0.15 / Vello 0.12 · winit 0.31.0-beta.4 · AccessKit 0.25 · Dioxus 0.7.3 · Boa 0.22 · tokio 1.42 · reqwest 0.13 — a native-API engine library with no server in a default build (the opt-in devtools feature's CDP server listens on 127.0.0.1) and no database (the browser app keeps a rusqlite 0.32 history); versions as `Cargo.toml` pins them.
- The workspace takes no git dependency — every crate a crates.io registry version with its checksum in the lockfile

- **Logged as-is elsewhere:** the upstream apps' `fmt::init()` and the WPT runner's `env_logger` carry visited URLs, resource URLs, link hrefs, element attributes, outer HTML of failed SVGs, CSS values and text-node contents unscrubbed. Past escher's scrub: std's panic hook prints the raw message, and `log.file` can carry a host path only for a bridged record under an engine target (recorded by construction, not measured). No record from a target outside the allowlist reaches stderr: both sink-installing binaries read no stable id and no accessible name at the default level, `info`, `debug` and `trace` — 0 lines at the default level, the one install line at the others (`escher-session` 1165 → 1 lines at `debug`, 1501 → 1 at `trace`; the windowed stand 12,413 → 1 and 47,482 → 1); the cost is that a third-party WARN or ERROR no longer prints. Typed text is measured in a host's log since 2026-10-10-driver-cli: a hosted `type` reaches the `escher-session` host's instance, and its stderr at `trace` holds 0 occurrences of a typed sentinel, 0 id needles and 0 name needles under both builds (`host_log`); by level, three commands on CRUD write 0 lines unset and 4 from `info` up on the host built alone — three command spans and the install line — and 6 on the workspace-built host, the `blitz_dom::document` INFO line printing twice (re-measured at 2026-10-14-stand-requirement-sweep). It was first measured in process — `stand_act_spans` drives the driver's commands with the sink over a capture at `info` and reads 0 occurrences of the supplied texts, 0 of 36 ids and 0 of 8 names; since 2026-10-14-quality-gates a client's own stderr, the host on flows beyond those three commands and the windowed stand built with the workspace, on the host's display, are measured too — 28 runs by build and level, 0 needles in every run (the client's a one-off reading). Since 2026-10-24-stand-requirement-sweep a recording session's clients are read by a standing check: `host_log`'s third test (unix only) runs each client command at `trace` — `start crud --record`, `type` with a sentinel, `snapshot`, `snapshot --part 1`, `lint`, `stop` — in `hl-client` and `hl-client-rec`, and over all the clients' own stderr reads 0 id, 0 name, 0 sentinel, 0 recording-path and 0 `recorded_needles` occurrences under both builds; a paged `part` read through the `escher-session` host's own sink is read by `host_log`'s fifth test (unix only), which runs `serve cells` at `RUST_LOG=trace` in `hl-cells`, commits a sentinel into a part-2 cell and calls `snapshot --part 2`: 0 id and 0 name needles under both builds, its failures naming a kind and a count only (`host_log` 5; measured at 2026-10-25-cold-agent-bar). A `multiple` select's chosen set leaves only as form entries — on `input` and `change` one `(name, FormValue::Text(value))` per chosen option (`multiple_select_values`) — as the snapshot's `value`, the first chosen option in tree order, and as the options' tree nodes, and a single list box's chosen row and row labels only in the snapshot, the diff and the actions answer, a select's chosen state never leaving as a log line, span or field, the added-lines census reading 0 (2026-10-31-engine-debts). `size` on a select, `multiple` or single, is an attribute read, parsed into a whole number capped at 65534, carrying no text out and moving no redaction shape, an engine change for every document and a boundary widening, ratified (2026-10-31-select-popup).
